ca_papa_boulder_2.blurb: Papa Boulder is a single large block in the Hemingway Boulders, a group of boulders in the Lost Horse part of Joshua Tree National Park. It is the first block a climber reaches on the walk in from the paved lot. Eight problems climb it, almost all at the easy end: one at the lowest grade, four at V0, two at V1 and a single V2. That spread keeps it to warm-up grades. The neighbouring blocks in the group add more problems in the same low range, which makes the whole cluster workable in a few hours.
ca_papa_boulder_2.approach: Level walk along the marked trail from the paved parking lot out across the flat desert floor.

ca_miledi_boulder.blurb: Miledi Boulder is one big block low on a rocky hillside in the Quail Springs side of Joshua Tree National Park, close to the road in from the west. It has eight problems with a wide spread: three at the lowest grade, one V0, then single problems at V3, V4, V5 and V6. Several of the lines are highballs, so pads and a spotter matter here, and the two best-known problems sit at V3 and V4. The block is tucked into the lee of the hillside, which breaks the wind. A short trail and a little easy scrambling bring you to its base, and the descent is the easy west side.
ca_miledi_boulder.parking_note: From the park entrance drive about two miles along the road; a dirt pullout on the right, just beyond the one used for the Scratch-N-Sniff Boulder, serves this boulder.
ca_miledi_boulder.approach: A trail runs from the pullout up the hillside to the block, with a little easy scrambling right at the end.

ca_horseshoe_slabs_boulder.blurb: This large boulder stands beside the path around Horseshoe Lake, at roughly 8,500 feet above Mammoth Lakes in the Eastern Sierra. It holds eight problems, none of them hard: two at the lowest grade, two at V1, three at V2 and one V3. The stone is compact, with the odd quartz vein, but many problems finish on high, delicate top-outs, so bring several pads and spotters. Tops can be dirty and clean up as more people climb. The boulder sits a short way past the Horseshoe Slabs along the same loop trail, and other boulders around the lake add to a day of bouldering.

ca_ok_corridor.blurb: OK Corridor is a narrow lane between tall boulders inside the Planet X bouldering zone in central Joshua Tree. Moderate problems are scarce elsewhere at Planet X, and this spot supplies a handful. Of its eight problems, three are at the lowest grade, two at V0, two at V1, and one is a much harder line near V9. A few of the problems are high, yet the ground beneath them is flat and clear. To find it, leave the western end of the Planet X boulders, follow the right branch of the trail and turn into the boulders opposite Newton's Law.

ca_mystical_stones.blurb: Mystical Stones is a cluster of boulders around a 40 ft roof crack, spread over the talus field coming off Mt. Dutzi near Echo Cove in Joshua Tree National Park. It has eight problems and runs harder than most of the surrounding blocks: two at V1, then one each at V3 and V4, three at V5 and one at V7. Two large boulders with dark patina mark the spot. Reaching them takes a walk on a trail to the chump clump formation, then some boulder hopping up the slope, so plan for uneven footing with your pads.

ca_lost_in_space.blurb: Lost In Space is a small set of granite boulders hidden among trees on the west side of Lake Tahoe, near Emerald Bay and within the Eagle Creek Canyon zone. There are eight problems, and most are hard: one at V1, then single problems at V5 and V6, two at V7, two at V8 and one V9. Getting there means roughly 15 to 20 minutes on the Eagle Lake trail, then across the creek and a couple more minutes to the blocks. Parking along this stretch fills up, so start early. The canyon's granite can bake in direct sun, which is worth remembering for a summer session.

ca_hooker_boot_wall.blurb: Hooker Boot Wall is a trad wall of about 75 feet in the Snow Play Walls group, off Highway 18 between Running Springs and Snow Valley in the San Bernardino Mountains. It is the biggest formation in that group and has the most routes, eight in all. Five go from 5.6 to 5.8, two are 5.10 and one is 5.11. Bolts are present, yet every route calls for a trad rack. Deep Creek runs beside the base, and the wall faces west.
ca_hooker_boot_wall.approach: Walk down the slope from the roadside parking area toward the creek; the wall is the first sizeable formation you reach. The hillside is loose underfoot.
